item.title: Statement by Spokesman Tommy Pigott on the Passing of His Majesty King Harald V of Norway
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson

Statement by Spokesman Tommy Pigott on the Passing of His Majesty King Harald V of Norway

Press Statement

August 29, 2026

On behalf of the people of the United States, I extend my deepest condolences to Her Majesty Queen Sonja, the entire Royal Family, and the Norwegian people on the passing of His Majesty King Harald V.

The King was a close friend of the United States and steadfast supporter of the strong relationship between our two countries. America was honored to provide a safe haven for the young Prince Harald and his family during the Second World War, and his subsequent royal visits across the United States strengthened the ties between our nations throughout his reign. King Harald’s personal commitment to celebrating the proud heritage of Norwegian-Americans and kinship between the people of the United States and Norway will forever serve as part of his enduring legacy.

item.title: Statement from Assistant Secretary Dylan Johnson on Revoking Visa from Iraqi National on FBI Terror Watchlist Given Award by Previous Administration
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Statement from Assistant Secretary Dylan Johnson on Revoking Visa from Iraqi National on FBI Terror Watchlist Given Award by Previous Administration

Media Note

August 28, 2026

The U.S. Department of State has revoked the visa of an Iraqi national who was presented an award by the Biden Administration for her purported role in fighting corruption and her advocacy for “gender equity.”

Taif Sami Mohammed Al Shakarchi was given the International Woman of Courage Award in 2022 by former Secretary of State Anthony Blinken and former First Lady Jill Biden.

The award recognized “women from around the globe who have demonstrated exceptional courage, strength, and leadership in advocating for peace, justice, human rights, gender equity and equality, and the empowerment of women and girls, in all their diversity.”

This Iraqi national’s visa has now been revoked by the State Department following her placement on the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Terror Watchlist. She is no longer present in the United States.

Under President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, suspected terrorists will never be allowed to remain in the United States.

item.title: U.S. Sanctions Sever Financial Lifelines of Iranian Regime
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson

U.S. Sanctions Sever Financial Lifelines of Iranian Regime

Press Statement

August 28, 2026

Operation Economic Outcast continues in full force. Today, the United States is imposing sanctions on the manager of the Dubai branch of Iran’s Bank Melli, Reza Mohammad Taeedi. Bank Melli has served as a critical financial hub for Iran’s armed forces, including the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force and the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics, both U.S.-sanctioned entities. We are also sanctioning a Hong Kong-based company that has helped designated Iranian individuals and entities to access the international financial system. In addition, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) proposed a rule that would revoke Banque Misr UAE’s correspondent banking access to U.S. financial institutions. Treasury assesses that Banque Misr UAE is a critical node for the Iranian regime’s access to U.S. dollars.

Today’s action intensifies our pressure campaign against Iran. As the regime prioritizes its malign activities above the needs of its people, we will sever the economic lifelines sustaining it. We will target individuals and entities that engage in illicit financial practices on behalf of the Iranian regime, including those working for Iranian banks outside the country.

Today’s sanctions actions are being taken pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, a counterterrorism authority, and E.O. 13902, which targets persons operating in Iran’s financial sector. FinCEN proposed its rule pursuant to section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.

item.title: Deputy Secretary Landau Travels to Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Kiribati
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Deputy Secretary Landau Travels to Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Kiribati

Media Note

August 28, 2026

Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau will travel to Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), Solomon Islands, and Kiribati from August 31 to September 11. In Palau, the Deputy Secretary will participate in the Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) Leaders’ Meeting with Forum Dialogue Partners to strengthen ties between the United States and Pacific Islands governments. In FSM and Solomon Islands, he will meet with government representatives and business leaders to further advance our shared economic and security priorities. In Kiribati, he will attend the Kiribati Development Partners Forum and meet with government representatives.

The Deputy Secretary will be joined on the trip to Palau, Federated States of Micronesia and Solomon Islands by U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Commandant Admiral Kevin Lunday, in recognition of the key role the Coast Guard plays in advancing regional maritime security. He will also be joined in Palau at the PIF by other U.S. interagency partners, including U.S. Pacific Command Deputy Commander Lieutenant General George Rowell and U.S. Department of the Interior Assistant Secretary Bill Hague.

The Pacific region remains an enduring foreign policy priority for the United States. The United States has deep and long-standing ties to the countries in the Pacific, who are not only our neighbors but also our friends. The United States is committed to engaging our Pacific Island partners to preserve an open, secure, and prosperous Pacific region.

item.title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Japanese Vice Foreign Minister Funakoshi
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Japanese Vice Foreign Minister Funakoshi

Readout

August 27, 2026

The below is attributable to Spokesman Tommy Pigott:

Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met today with Japanese Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs Funakoshi Takehiro. The Deputy Secretary and the Vice Minister reaffirmed the importance of the U.S.-Japan Alliance and their strong opposition to any actions that undermine regional peace and stability. They reiterated their shared commitment to bolstering deterrence to advance a free and open Indo-Pacific.

The senior officials also discussed the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, including the importance of freedom of navigation, and their shared commitment to enhancing global economic security by strengthening secure, reliable supply chains across key industries.

item.title: Moldova National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Moldova National Day

Press Statement

August 27, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the people of Moldova on the anniversary of their independence.

The United States is proud to continue strengthening our partnership with Moldova. Over the past year, our two countries have deepened cooperation across a range of shared priorities. We have expanded economic ties, strengthened border security, and worked together to promote stability in the region.

As Moldova celebrates 35 years of freedom, the United States remains committed to supporting the Moldovan people’s sovereignty and independence. On this day, I extend my warmest wishes to the people of Moldova for continued peace, prosperity, and progress.

item.title: United States Expresses Condolences to the Victims of the Nepal Floods
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

United States Expresses Condolences to the Victims of the Nepal Floods

Media Note

August 26, 2026

The United States extends its deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in the devastating flash floods in the Rasuwa district of Nepal. Our thoughts are with all those affected by this disaster.

The State Department is closely monitoring the situation and is deploying a disaster response advisor to the region to support response efforts. The Department will also provide $500,000 in assistance through its global award with Catholic Relief Services, supporting emergency shelter, relief items, and water, sanitation, and hygiene assistance to flood-affected communities.

The U.S. Embassy in Kathmandu is working closely with local authorities to locate and assist U.S. citizens in the affected areas. U.S. citizens in Nepal who need urgent assistance related to the flooding should contact the U.S. Embassy at KathmanduACS@state.gov. We strongly encourage U.S. citizens in the affected areas to monitor local news, follow instructions from local authorities, and enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) at step.state.gov to receive important safety and emergency information.

Concerned U.S. citizens seeking information about family members in Nepal should call 1-888-407-4747 toll-free from the United States and Canada, or 1-202-501-4444 from other locations.

item.title: Fifth Anniversary of the Attack at Abbey Gate
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Fifth Anniversary of the Attack at Abbey Gate

Press Statement

August 26, 2026

Today marks five years since the horrific attack at Kabul Airport’s Abbey Gate, a tragedy that resulted in the deaths of 13 American heroes and over 160 Afghan civilians.

We stand with the Gold Star families whose loved ones made the ultimate sacrifice in service to our great country. Our prayers will forever remain with them and the 45 U.S. service members who were injured during this terrible terrorist attack.

The Biden Administration’s disastrous withdrawal from Afghanistan remains a dark stain on our nation’s history. The Trump Administration remains dedicated to honoring the memory of those who lost their lives at Abbey Gate – and during the country’s 20 years in Afghanistan – and providing the American people with the answers they deserve.

item.title: State Department Announces Intent to Appoint Directors to the United States Foundation for Natural Security and Counterterrorism
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

State Department Announces Intent to Appoint Directors to the United States Foundation for Natural Security and Counterterrorism

Media Note

August 26, 2026

The Department of State today announced Secretary Rubio’s intent to appoint four distinguished Americans to serve as Directors on the Board of the United States Foundation for Natural Security and Counterterrorism (USFNSC): Samuel Robson Walton, L. Daniel Hammond, Joseph C. Semsar, and Dr. Ari Novy.

Samuel Robson Walton

Samuel Robson “Rob” Walton is the Founder of the Rob Walton Foundation and is an owner with his family of the Denver Broncos. He previously served as Chairman of Walmart from 1992 to 2015, helping grow the company into a global brand and one of the world’s largest enterprises. Through the Rob Walton Foundation, Walton has supported efforts to protect terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems.

L. Daniel Hammond

L. Daniel “Dan” Hammond is the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of American Hometown Media, where he leads a portfolio of community-focused media brands celebrating positive stories from across America. Prior to that he founded and led Publishing Group of America which produced the largest successful magazine launch in U.S. history, and American Hometown Publishing, the largest owner-operator of community newspapers in the Southeast. An avid outdoorsman, Hammond has a longstanding connection to hunting, conservation, and responsible land stewardship. He served the past 25 years as a Board Member of the Tennessee Wildlife Federation.

Joseph C. Semsar

Joseph “Joe” C. Semsar is Head of Sovereign AI at Reflection AI, where he leads the company’s work with governments and strategic partners to build secure, sovereign artificial intelligence capabilities that advance national competitiveness, resilience, and technological leadership. His work sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, national security, economic policy, and public-private partnerships. Semsar previously served as a senior executive at the New York Stock Exchange and as Under Secretary of Commerce for International Trade during the first Trump Administration.

Dr. Ari Novy

Dr. Ari Novy is the Elizabeth Newman Wilds Executive Director of Cornell Botanic Gardens. A plant biologist by training, Novy previously served as President and CEO of the San Diego Botanic Garden and as Executive Director of the United States Botanic Garden in Washington, D.C. He has held academic and advisory appointments with institutions including the Salk Institute for Biological Studies and has contributed to national and international initiatives focused on plant conservation and environmental policy.

The Department looks forward to working with these four qualified individuals on the USFNSC Board to establish the Foundation as a durable, results-oriented vehicle for American leadership in natural resource security and conservation. By effectively pairing private philanthropy with U.S. government efforts, the Foundation can support partner country activities to protect some of the world’s most important ecosystems under their own national jurisdiction while strengthening cooperation, promoting peace and prosperity, and advancing U.S. interests abroad.

The appointments are subject to completion of all applicable processes and requirements.
